subject: Spike in latency and increased completion variance after v4beta quant rollout
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@tesserahealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Devon Patel <devon.patel@tesserahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0500
Subject: Spike in latency + completion variance after v4beta quant rollout

Nikhil / Marcus —

We rolled the v4beta quantized profile this morning at ~08:30 PT across our prod tenant (per the playbook). Since then we've seen P99 latency jump from ~320ms to ~1.1s and a noticeable increase in incorrect/garbled completions for our consent-extraction flows (~3x baseline error rate).

This is impacting customer-facing flows and billing is on hold for customers affected. We're attaching a small sample of request IDs and timestamps. Can you confirm whether this rollout included the latest KV cache changes or if a new kernel selection was introduced?

Urgent ask: please escalate to your infra/runtime team and advise mitigation steps — rollback, routing to non-quantized variant, or temporary throttling would all be acceptable stops while we stabilize.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Dir, Platform Engineering
Tessera Health

Attachments: tessera_request_ids.csv (list of 120 request ids, timestamps)

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@tesserahealth.com>, Devon Patel <devon.patel@tesserahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 09:34:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Spike in latency + completion variance after v4beta quant rollout

Samantha —

Thanks for the heads up and for the sample IDs. I pulled the first 20 and we've already flagged them to runtime. Initial hypothesis: the v4beta quant profile changed kernel selection for medium-length contexts and introduced a path that degrades prefix-cache hit behavior under your traffic pattern. That could explain the p99 and the variance.

Immediate plan (next 90 minutes):
- I will request an emergency routing rule to send Tessera traffic to the v4alpha-nq (non-quant) model variant while we investigate.
- Marcus will coordinate infra for a fast rollback option if the routing shift isn't sufficient.
- Please share any examples of prompts where the output is incorrect — that will help validate whether this is a decode/regression vs. sampling miscalibration.

We will keep you updated every 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we consider this a P1 and will engage execs if mitigation doesn't hold.

Nikhil
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

> > Attachments: tessera_request_ids.csv

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 10:05:00 -05:00
Subject: ACTION: Tessera P1 — route to non-quant variant and quick mitigations

Team —

FYI: Tessera (DEAL-48921) is seeing p99 up ~3.5x and error/garbled completions after v4beta quant rollout. Customer is P1; they've paused billing for affected customers. I called Marcus to flag infra.

Proposed immediate steps (I will own comms to customer):
1) Router change: route 100% of tesserahealth.com traffic to v4alpha-nq (non-quant) for 2 hours. This is a soft rollback at the routing layer only (no node redeploy).
2) Runtime: pin kernel selection to the previous kernel set for medium contexts while we run A/B with saved traces.
3) Observability: increase sampling for KV-hit traces for Tessera requests and dump decoder logits for 1% of requests.
4) Billing: propose a 10% credit for impacted hour window if we cannot meet SLOs — Marcus to advise finance/legal.

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.md — contains step-by-step router and runtime commands.

Risks/costs: routing to non-quant will raise token cost ~2.3x for their workload but should restore correctness and latency. Need approval for burst capacity if active traffic rises.

Please ack and execute the Router change asap; Marcus, can you push infra ticket and confirm ETA? Grace/Evelyn, can you monitor the model quality dashboards and flag any residual drift after routing change?

Nikhil

> On Tue, Feb 23, 2027 at 09:34 AM Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com> wrote:
> > Immediate plan (next 90 minutes):...

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 10:19:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: ACTION: Tessera P1 — route to non-quant variant and quick mitigations

Acked. Infra is standing by.

I'll open an Emergency Ops ticket (OPS-8721) and ask infra to apply the router override; ETA < 20m. If routing change does not measurably drop p99 within 15min we'll schedule a node-level rollback to the previous v4alpha kernel set (will require a short rolling restart window).

On the exec front: recommend we prep a one-pager for the CRO/VP Products with timeline, mitigation, and a recommended credit. If the customer pauses billing we should be ready to offer a commercial concession while we stabilize. Evelyn — can you draft the one-pager? Grace — stands up quality probes and share a sample diff.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference

From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@tesserahealth.com>, Devon Patel <devon.patel@tesserahealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Feb 2027 13:45:00 -05:00
Subject: Mitigation in place — routing to v4alpha-nq, next steps

Samantha / Devon —

Quick update: routing override applied at 13:15 ET (router rule ID R-9834) — Tessera traffic is now flowing to v4alpha-nq. Early telemetry shows p99 down to ~340ms and error rate trending back toward baseline. We will keep the override for 2 hours while we collect the higher-fidelity traces.

Requests for you:
- Please upload 10-20 failing prompt/response pairs to the shared Drive folder (link below) so our ML team can reproduce decoding failures.
- If you can, share peak QPS windows from this morning so we can correlate load patterns.

Next steps from our side:
- Grace to share a diff report within 60m comparing decoder logits and KV-hit rates between v4beta and v4alpha-nq for your sample IDs.
- Marcus to prepare the one-pager for the CRO with mitigation timeline and proposed 10% credit for affected hours.
- We will follow up with an RCA and a proposal for a safer rollout process for quant profiles (staged canary + model-swap policy).

Drive link: https://drive.redwoodinternal.com/teams/ops/tessera-v4beta-incident
Ops ticket: OPS-8721
HubSpot: hubspot:4938202

Apologies again for the impact — I'll escalate to the execs if we see any re-regression.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation_playbook_v1.md (router commands, playback steps)
